item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00294","decision":"none","candidate_ranking":["C07","C11","C10"],"selected_candidate_label":null,"confidence":0.98,"relationship_type":"none","rationale":"The strongest candidates concern Selective Service treatment of persons with criminal convictions and persons honorably separated from military service, but none uses the child's distinctive pardon machinery: invocation of the constitutional pardon power, a class-wide grant of a full pardon, eligibility based on pre-service federal convictions plus a specified period of honorable active service, and an exclusion for post-entry convictions. The overlap is therefore subject-matter terminology rather than evidence of a concrete drafting template.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"persons who had prior to their entry, enrollment, or induction been convicted of offenses against the laws of the United States","parent_excerpt":"who has been convicted of a criminal offense which may be punished by death or by imprisonment for a term exceeding one year","explanation":"C07 addresses convicted registrants, but only as part of a Selective Service classification rule; it provides no pardon or analogous relief mechanism."},{"child_excerpt":"have been or shall hereafter be honorably discharged or separated therefrom, or separated under honorable conditions from active service therein","parent_excerpt":"has been separated therefrom by honorable discharge or discharge under honorable conditions or by an equivalent type of release from service","explanation":"C11 shares relatively close military-separation terminology, but that language defines a Selective Service classification and does not structure the later pardon."},{"child_excerpt":"after serving in active status for not less than one year subsequent to June 25, 1950","parent_excerpt":"served honorably on active duty between September 16, 1940, and June 24, 1948, for a period of 90 days or more but less than 12 months","explanation":"C10 likewise uses service dates, duration, and honorable-service criteria, but these are routine eligibility elements in military regulations rather than substantially the same legal machinery."}]}
